cohort: Infants born to women with suspected or confirmed Zika virus infection during pregnancy, including those with microcephaly at birth and those with possible congenital ZIKV exposure who appeared well at birth.
finding: In the Dominican Republic epidemic, 11% of infants born to women with suspected or confirmed ZIKV during pregnancy had microcephaly, and 4% of ZIKV-exposed infants developed postnatal neurocognitive abnormalities persisting up to 15-18 months.
